items.q: The four histological variants of FSGS listed are classical, 2° perihilar, tip variant and:
items.exp: Variants: classical, 2° perihilar, tip variant, collapsing FSGS. (Book p767)

items.q: The tip variant FSGS is described with lesion only at tip, features like MCD and:
items.exp: Tip variant: lesion only at tip; features like MCD; good prognosis. (Book p767)

items.q: The FSGS variant carrying the worst prognosis is:
Collapsing FSGS is associated with HIV/HIVAN, heroin, IFN α, parvo virus B19 and:
items.exp: Associated with: HIV, HIVAN, heroin, IFN α, parvo virus B19, pamidronate. (Book p767)

items.q: Collapsing FSGS shows complete collapse of glomeruli with hypertrophy of podocyte, nicknamed:
items.exp: Complete collapse of glomeruli with hypertrophy of podocyte (pseudocrescent); dilated tubules & microcysts. (Book p767)

items.q: On electron microscopy, collapsing FSGS shows dilated cisternae of endoplasmic reticulum termed:
items.exp: Electron microscope: dilated cisternae of endoplasmic reticulum (IFN footprints). (Book p767)

items.q: The note distinguishes the pseudocrescent of collapsing FSGS from the true crescent, which is:
items.exp: Hypertrophy of parietal epithelial cell: true crescent. (Book p767)

items.q: Conditions listed with the IFN footprint are SLE and:
items.exp: Condition with IFN footprint: SLE; FSGS (collapsing variant). (Book p767)

items.q: All of the following are associated with collapsing FSGS EXCEPT:
items.exp: Collapsing associations: HIV/HIVAN, heroin, IFN α, parvo B19, pamidronate; gold is an MN drug. (Book p767)

items.q: Which crescent statement is TRUE as per the note?
opts: Hypertrophy of parietal epithelial cell is the true crescent, while podocyte hypertrophy in collapsing FSGS is a pseudocrescent
Podocyte hypertrophy forms the true crescent
Parietal cell hypertrophy forms the pseudocrescent
items.exp: Parietal epithelial cell hypertrophy = true crescent; collapsing podocyte hypertrophy = pseudocrescent. (Book p767)
